newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Minister says Australia seeks more mobile army.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Minister says Australia seeks more mobile army.

text.p: Australia will restructure its army to create a more mobile force better suited to its vast, empty continent, Defence Minister Ian McLachlan announced on Thursday.

"... The present structure of the army is not suited to our need for highly mobile operations, with forces dispersed over vast stretches of land," McLachlan said, detailing a Defence Department report in a speech to former defence personnel.

"I have drawn on elements of the report in developing a new structure for the army which, by 2000, will give us a force more mobile, better trained, better equipped and shaped to fight on the modern battlefield -- wherever that battlefield may be."
The new conservative government, elected in March, has also announced a policy of cutting defence administration to boost fighting strength -- increasing the teeth-to-tail ratio, in military jargon.
The Australian army is already a relatively light and mobile force by the standards of developed countries.
It has little heavy equipment such as tanks and large-calibre artillery.
